questions.text: What are trousers made of tough cotton twill called, often dyed blue?
questions.explanation: Denim jeans were popularised by Levi Strauss and Co. in the 19th century.

questions.text: What colour is the traditional Western wedding dress?
questions.explanation: The white wedding dress was popularised after Queen Victoria's 1840 wedding.

questions.text: Which fabric is made from the fleece of sheep?
questions.explanation: Wool is shorn, spun and woven or knitted.

Which Italian city is famed for its major fashion week and houses such as Prada and Armani?
questions.explanation: Milan Fashion Week is one of the 'big four'.

questions.text: Which designer launched the 'New Look' in 1947?
questions.explanation: The New Look had a nipped waist and full skirt.

questions.text: Which British designer is credited with popularising the miniskirt in the 1960s?
questions.explanation: Quant's boutique Bazaar was on the King's Road, Chelsea.

questions.text: Which Swedish company, founded in 1943 by Ingvar Kamprad, is famous for flat-pack furniture?
questions.explanation: IKEA's name comes from the founder's initials and his home farm and village.

questions.text: Which German design school was founded by Walter Gropius in 1919?
questions.explanation: The Bauhaus was founded in Weimar.

questions.text: Which Italian fashion house, founded in 1921 in Florence, uses a double-G logo?
questions.explanation: Guccio Gucci opened the first shop in Florence.

questions.text: Who designed the Barcelona chair, introduced in 1929?
questions.explanation: It was designed for the German Pavilion at the Barcelona International Exposition.

questions.text: Which Spanish couturier opened a Paris fashion house in 1937 and was known for sculptural cuts?
questions.explanation: Balenciaga was admired as a master of cut and construction.

questions.text: Which Danish designer created the Egg and Swan chairs?
questions.explanation: Jacobsen designed them for the SAS Royal Hotel in Copenhagen.

questions.text: Which designer introduced the women's tuxedo suit 'Le Smoking' in 1966?
questions.explanation: Le Smoking was a landmark of androgynous fashion.

spares.text: Which item of clothing keeps your neck warm in winter?
spares.explanation: A scarf is wrapped around the neck.

spares.text: Which pattern of checks is traditionally associated with Scottish kilts?
spares.explanation: Tartans are linked to Scottish clans and districts.

spares.text: Which Italian designer founded his fashion house in 1975 and is known for relaxed tailoring?
spares.explanation: Armani founded the label with Sergio Galeotti in Milan.

spares.text: Which Finnish-American architect designed the Tulip chair and the Gateway Arch?
spares.explanation: Saarinen designed both in the mid-20th century.
